questions.q: In Bela's Building of Fun, the ground floor is called Floor 0. Which statement about the number 0 is correct?
questions.a: 0 is neither a positive nor a negative number.
o: 0 is neither a positive nor a negative number.
0 is a positive number, because it is above the floors below the ground.
0 is a negative number, because it is below the floors above the ground.
0 is both a positive and a negative number.

questions.q: A hotel in Hyderabad numbers its floors with the ground floor as Floor 0. Its car park is three floors below the ground floor. What is the floor number of the car park?
questions.a: Floor -3

questions.q:
In a building whose ground floor is Floor 0, match each floor in Column I with its floor number in Column II.
Column I: I. Two floors below the ground floor  II. The ground floor  III. Four floors above the ground floor  IV. One floor below the ground floor
Column II: A. 0  B. -1  C. +4  D. -2
questions.a: I-D, II-A, III-C, IV-B

questions.q: (a) Write the integers 4, -9, -1, 6 and -5 in decreasing order. (b) Which of them is the greatest negative number?
questions.a: (a) 6, 4, -1, -5, -9. (b) -1, because it lies to the right of the other negative numbers -5 and -9 on the number line.
s: (b) Names -1 as the greatest negative number

questions.q: True or false: Every negative number is less than every positive number. Give the reason or the correct statement.
questions.a: True. Every negative number is less than 0 (its floor is below Floor 0) and every positive number is greater than 0 (its floor is above Floor 0), so any negative number is less than any positive number.
s: Reason: negative numbers are less than 0 and positive numbers are greater than 0 (below and above Floor 0)

questions.q:
Assertion (A): -12 < -3.
Reason (R): Of two negative numbers, the one with the bigger number after the minus sign is the greater number.
questions.a: A is true but R is false.
o: A is true but R is false.
Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is false but R is true.

questions.q:
In a tall building the ground floor is Floor 0. Riya is on Floor -6. Kunal is 4 floors above Riya, and Meena is 9 floors above Kunal.
(a) On which floor is Kunal?
(b) On which floor is Meena?
(c) Write the three floors in increasing order and say who is closest to the ground floor.
questions.a: (a) Kunal is on Floor -2 (4 floors up from -6). (b) Meena is on Floor +7 (9 floors up from -2). (c) -6 < -2 < +7, so Riya, Kunal, Meena from lowest to highest; Kunal is closest to the ground floor, only 2 floors away.
s: (c) Orders -6 < -2 < +7 and names Kunal as closest to Floor 0

questions.q: Farhan says, 'If one number is less than another, then the inverse of the first number is also less than the inverse of the second.' Test his claim with the pairs (-5, 2) and (-7, -3), and say whether he is right.
questions.a: For -5 < 2 the inverses are 5 and -2, and 5 > -2. For -7 < -3 the inverses are 7 and 3, and 7 > 3. In both pairs the order turns round, so Farhan is wrong: taking inverses reverses the order, because each inverse sits on the opposite side of 0 at the same distance.
s: Concludes the claim is wrong because taking inverses reverses the order

questions.q: On a number line, p is 3 steps to the left of 0, q is 5 steps to the left of p, r is 7 steps to the right of q, and s is the inverse of r. Which ordering is correct?
questions.a: q < p < r < s

questions.q:
A shopping complex in Lucknow has a lift that serves every floor from Floor -4 up to Floor +9; the ground floor is Floor 0. There are two parking levels: P1 on Floor -1 with 60 spaces and P2 on Floor -3 with 120 spaces. The cinema is on Floor +7. On a weekday about 90 cars come, and the manager can keep only ONE parking level open to save on lights and guards.
(a) Which parking level is lower? Write the comparison using < or >.
(b) How many floors does the lift serve in all, counting the ground floor?
(c) How many floors must the lift go up to take a visitor from P2 to the cinema?
(d) Which parking level should the manager keep open on weekdays? Give one reason for your choice and one thing it costs the visitors.
questions.a: (a) P2 is lower, since -3 < -1. (b) Floors -4 to -1, 0 and +1 to +9 make 4 + 1 + 9 = 14 floors. (c) From -3 to +7 is 10 floors up (+10). (d) P2: P1 has only 60 spaces, so 30 of the 90 cars would find no space; P2 has room for all of them. The cost is that P2 visitors travel 2 floors more (10 floors to the cinema instead of 8 from P1).
s: (d) Chooses P2 because 60 spaces cannot hold 90 cars, and notes the extra 2 floors of travel

questions.q: Asha is on Floor -2 of a building and presses +5 in the lift. On which floor does she arrive?
questions.a: Floor +3

questions.q: What is the inverse of -14?
Which addition has the same value as (+9) - (-4)?

A lift is on Floor -3 and has to reach Floor +4.
(a) Which button press is needed?
(b) Write this as a subtraction in the form Target Floor - Starting Floor = Movement needed.
questions.a: (a) +7 (seven floors up). (b) (+4) - (-3) = +7.

questions.q:
On a number line, Sonu stands at 35 and walks to -15.
(a) Write the subtraction that gives the movement needed.
(b) Find the movement and say in which direction he walks.
questions.a: (a) (-15) - 35. (b) The movement is -50: he walks 50 steps to the left (backward).
s: (b) Finds -50 and says 50 steps to the left

questions.q:
In a mine the ground level is 0 and levels are measured in metres. A cage starts at a loading platform at +60 m. It goes down 135 m to pick up miners, and then goes down 50 m more.
(a) At which level is the cage after the first movement?
(b) At which level is it after the second movement?
(c) Using Target Level - Starting Level, find the movement needed to bring it straight back to the platform.

Assertion (A): (-6) - (+10) = -16.
Reason (R): Subtracting a number gives the same result as adding its inverse.
questions.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements.
I. (+15) - (-5) = (+15) + (-5).
II. (-4) - (+7) = (-4) + (-7).
III. (-8) - (-2) = -6.
Which of the statements are correct?
questions.a: II and III only

questions.q:
A lift attendant starts on Floor -4. He presses +9, then -12, then +5.
(a) Write one addition expression for the whole trip, starting from Floor -4.
(b) On which floor does he end?
(c) Which single press would have taken him from Floor -4 to the same floor?
(d) From the final floor, which press takes him back to Floor -4, and how is it related to your answer to (c)?
questions.a: (a) (-4) + (+9) + (-12) + (+5). (b) Floor -2. (c) (+9) + (-12) + (+5) = +2, so a single press of +2. (d) He must press -2, since (-4) - (-2) = -2. This is the inverse of +2: pressing a movement and then its inverse brings the lift back to where it started.
s: (c) Combines the presses into a single +2
(d) Gives -2 and says it is the inverse of +2

questions.q:
Ananya says, 'When you subtract, the answer is always smaller than the number you started with.'
(a) Find 12 - 5, 12 - (-5), (-12) - (-5) and (-12) - 5.
(b) In which of these four is the answer smaller than the starting number?
(c) State when Ananya's claim is true and when it is false.
(d) Explain, using Target - Starting = Movement or the lift, why subtracting a negative number gives a bigger answer.
questions.a: (a) 7, 17, -7 and -17. (b) Only 12 - 5 = 7 and (-12) - 5 = -17 are smaller than the starting numbers 12 and -12; 17 > 12 and -7 > -12. (c) Her claim is true when a positive number is subtracted and false when a negative number is subtracted. (d) Subtracting a negative number is the same as adding the corresponding positive number, e.g. 12 - (-5) = 12 + 5; in the lift that is pressing '+' and going up, so the answer is greater.
s: (c) Says the claim holds for subtracting a positive number and fails for a negative one
(d) Explains that subtracting a negative equals adding the positive, so the lift goes up

questions.q: In the token model, what is a 'zero pair'?
questions.a: A positive token and a negative token together
o: A positive token and a negative token together
Two positive tokens placed side by side
Two negative tokens placed side by side
Any two tokens that have the same colour

questions.q: A pile has 6 green (positive) tokens and 11 red (negative) tokens. What is the value of the pile?
With tokens, you start with the tokens of the first number only and then take away the tokens of the second number. Which subtraction can be done WITHOUT putting in any zero pairs?
(a) What is a zero pair in the token model? (b) Describe a pile of 6 tokens whose value is zero.
questions.a: (a) A zero pair is one positive (green) token and one negative (red) token together; they cancel, so the pair has value zero. (b) 3 green and 3 red tokens: they form 3 zero pairs, so the value is 0.
s: (a) Defines a zero pair as one green and one red token with value zero

questions.q: True or false: Putting extra zero pairs into a pile of tokens changes the value of the pile. Give the reason or the correct statement.
questions.a: False. Each zero pair has value zero, so putting in zero pairs does not change the value of the pile; this is why we may add them before subtracting.
s: Reason: a zero pair is worth 0, so the value of the pile stays the same

questions.q:
Use tokens to find each value. Say how many zero pairs you cancel or put in.
(a) (+8) + (-5)
(b) (-3) - (-7)
(c) (+1) - (+6)
questions.a: (a) 8 green and 5 red: cancel 5 zero pairs, 3 green are left, so +3. (b) 3 red: put in 4 zero pairs (7 red, 4 green), take out 7 red, 4 green are left, so +4. (c) 1 green: put in 5 zero pairs (6 green, 5 red), take out 6 green, 5 red are left, so -5.
s: (b) Puts in 4 zero pairs and gets +4
(c) Puts in 5 zero pairs and gets -5

questions.q: A pile of 11 tokens, some green (positive) and some red (negative), has the value -3. How many green tokens are in the pile?

Each subtraction in Column I is done with tokens: you start with the tokens of the first number only. Match it with the least number of zero pairs you must put in, from Column II.
Column I: I. (+4) - (+9)  II. (-2) - (+3)  III. (+5) - (-1)  IV. (-6) - (-2)
Column II: A. 0  B. 1  C. 3  D. 5
questions.a: I-D, II-C, III-B, IV-A

questions.q: Arjun says, 'If a pile has more red tokens than green tokens, its value is negative. And if I put in enough zero pairs, I can make such a pile positive.' Check both parts of his statement and give your verdict.
questions.a: The first part is right: each green token cancels one red token, and the red tokens left over make the value negative. The second part is wrong: each zero pair adds one green and one red token, so the red tokens still outnumber the green ones by the same number. For example, 2 green and 5 red is -3; with 10 zero pairs it is 12 green and 15 red, still -3. So Arjun is only partly right.
s: Agrees with the first part: the leftover red tokens make the value negative
Shows the second part fails: a zero pair adds one of each colour (with an example where the value stays the same)

questions.q:
In a class game in Guwahati each team starts with an empty bag. For every '+' card a team draws, it puts a green (positive) token in its bag; for every '-' card, a red (negative) token. After the first round Team A has 14 green and 9 red tokens, Team B has 7 green and 15 red tokens, and Team C has 12 green and 12 red tokens.
(a) What is the value of Team A's bag?
(b) What is the value of Team B's bag?
(c) Team C's bag has 24 tokens. Why is its value 0?
(d) In the final only Teams A and B play, and the bag closer to 0 wins. Before the final, Team B may make ONE move: put in 8 zero pairs, put in 4 green tokens, or take out 4 red tokens. Which move or moves let Team B win? Explain.
questions.a: (a) 9 zero pairs cancel, leaving 5 green tokens: +5. (b) 7 zero pairs cancel, leaving 8 red: -8. (c) Its 12 green and 12 red tokens make 12 zero pairs, each worth 0, so the bag is worth 0. (d) Putting in 8 zero pairs leaves the value -8, which is 8 away from 0 and loses to Team A (5 away). Putting in 4 green tokens gives 11 green and 15 red, -4; taking out 4 red gives 7 green and 11 red, also -4. Either of these two moves puts Team B 4 away from 0, closer than Team A, so either one wins.
s: (c) Explains that 12 zero pairs are worth 0
(d) Shows zero pairs leave -8 but both other moves give -4, which beats +5

questions.q: In a bank account, credits are written as positive numbers and debits as negative numbers. Which pair shows a credit of Rs 300 and then a debit of Rs 300?
Heights above sea level are positive and depths below sea level are negative. A diver is at -12 m and goes down 9 m more. At what height is she now?
True or false: A point 200 m below sea level is higher than a point 50 m below sea level, because 200 is greater than 50. Give the reason or the correct statement.
questions.a: False. The two heights are -200 m and -50 m, and -200 < -50, so the point 200 m below sea level is LOWER than the point 50 m below sea level.
s: Writes the heights as -200 and -50 and shows -200 < -50, so it is lower

questions.q:
A weather station in Ladakh records the lowest temperature on five days of a winter week: Monday -6 degrees Celsius, Tuesday -9, Wednesday -2, Thursday 0 and Friday -11.
(a) Which day was the coldest?
(b) Which day was the warmest?
(c) Write the five temperatures in increasing order.
(d) How many degrees warmer was Wednesday than Tuesday?
(e) Saturday's lowest temperature was 4 degrees higher than Friday's. What was it?
questions.a: (a) Friday (-11 degrees Celsius). (b) Thursday (0 degrees Celsius). (c) -11, -9, -6, -2, 0. (d) (-2) - (-9) = 7 degrees warmer. (e) (-11) + 4 = -7 degrees Celsius.

questions.q:
A school canteen in Coimbatore keeps a bank account. On Monday morning the balance is Rs 1,500. The entries for the week are: Monday, a debit of Rs 2,100 for vegetables; Tuesday, a credit of Rs 900 from sales; Wednesday, a debit of Rs 450 for gas; Thursday, a credit of Rs 1,800 from sales. The bank allows a negative balance for a short time, but on Friday morning it takes a fee of Rs 50 for every day that ended with a negative balance.
(a) What is the balance at the end of Monday?
(b) What is the balance at the end of Tuesday?
(c) What are the balances at the end of Wednesday and of Thursday?
(d) How much fee does the bank take on Friday, and what is the balance after it?
questions.a: (a) 1,500 - 2,100 = -Rs 600. (b) -600 + 900 = Rs 300. (c) Wednesday: 300 - 450 = -Rs 150; Thursday: -150 + 1,800 = Rs 1,650. (d) Two days (Monday and Wednesday) ended negative, so the fee is 2 x Rs 50 = Rs 100, and the balance becomes 1,650 - 100 = Rs 1,550.
s: (d) Counts 2 negative days, fee Rs 100, balance Rs 1,550

questions.q:
A submarine is at -180 m (180 m below sea level). It rises 75 m and then dives 130 m.
(a) Write one expression for its final position and find it.
(b) How many metres must it then rise to reach -50 m?
s: (a) Writes the expression and finds -235 m

questions.q:
A geographical cross section shows four points measured from sea level: P at 1,250 m above, Q at 340 m below, R at 60 m above and S at 910 m below.
(a) Write the heights as integers and arrange the points in decreasing order of height.
(b) Find the vertical distance between the highest and the lowest point.
(c) How much higher is R than Q?
s: (a) Writes the integers and orders P, R, Q, S

questions.q:
Assertion (A): -15 degrees Celsius is colder than -5 degrees Celsius.
Reason (R): Temperatures below the freezing point of water are written as negative numbers.
questions.a: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
o: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

questions.q:
A shopkeeper in Surat has Rs 2,500 in her bank account. A supplier offers her stock worth Rs 6,000 if she pays today. Her bank lets the balance go negative for a short time but then charges a fee of Rs 100. Tomorrow she will receive Rs 9,000 from a customer. If she waits and pays tomorrow, the supplier will charge Rs 300 more.
(a) What is her balance today if she pays now?
(b) If she pays now, what is her balance tomorrow after the fee and the customer's payment?
(c) What is her balance tomorrow if she waits and pays tomorrow instead?
(d) Which plan leaves her with more money, and by how much?
questions.a: (a) 2,500 - 6,000 = -Rs 3,500. (b) -3,500 - 100 + 9,000 = Rs 5,400. (c) 2,500 + 9,000 - 6,300 = Rs 5,200. (d) Paying now leaves Rs 200 more, because the Rs 100 fee is smaller than the Rs 300 extra charge for waiting.
s: (b) Finds Rs 5,400 after the fee and the credit
(d) Decides that paying now is better by Rs 200, comparing the fee with the extra charge

questions.q: At midnight four hill towns record these temperatures in degrees Celsius: W -6, X 3, Y -11 and Z 1. By noon, W has risen 8 degrees, X 4 degrees, Y 15 degrees and Z 2 degrees. Which town is the warmest at noon?
questions.a: Town X

questions.q: The top row of a border integer square reads 6, -2, -7. What is the border sum of the square?
Which list shows all the integers between -6 and -1, in increasing order?

Look at the sequence 20, 14, 8, 2, ___, ___.
(a) What number is added to each term to get the next one?
(b) Write the next two terms.
questions.a: (a) -6 is added each time (each term is 6 less). (b) 2 + (-6) = -4 and -4 + (-6) = -10.
s: (a) States that -6 is added each time

questions.q:
A 3 by 3 border integer square has these numbers. Top row: 2, -5, 0. Left column (top to bottom): 2, 4, -9. Right column (top to bottom): 0, a blank, 1. Bottom row (left to right): -9, a blank, 1.
(a) Find the border sum from the top row.
(b) Fill the blank in the right column.
(c) Fill the blank in the bottom row.
questions.a: (a) 2 + (-5) + 0 = -3 (the left column 2 + 4 + (-9) = -3 agrees). (b) 0 + ? + 1 = -3, so the blank is -4. (c) (-9) + ? + 1 = -3, so the blank is 5.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements.
I. In a border integer square, the top row, the bottom row, the leftmost column and the rightmost column all add up to the same border sum.
II. In the amazing grid game, after you circle a number you strike out its row and its column.
III. In a 3 by 3 border integer square, the number in the centre cell is part of the border sum.
Which of the statements are correct?
questions.a: I and II only

questions.q: Ravi plays the amazing grid game on this grid. Row 1: 1, 4, 7. Row 2: -2, 1, 4. Row 3: -5, -2, 1. He circles 7 first, then circles any unstruck number, and so on until no number is left. What is the total of his circled numbers?

Remember that there was no year 0: the year just before 1 CE is 1 BCE.
(a) Which year was 30 years after 10 BCE?
(b) Which year was 100 years before 40 CE?
questions.a: (a) 21 CE: from 10 BCE to 1 CE is 10 years, and 20 more years gives 21 CE. (b) 61 BCE: from 40 CE back to 1 BCE is 40 years, and 60 more years back gives 61 BCE.
s: (a) Gets 21 CE, allowing for no year 0
(b) Gets 61 BCE, allowing for no year 0

questions.q: Two dice each have the faces -1, 2, -3, 4, -5 and 6. Both dice are rolled and the two numbers are added. Show that the sum can never be 0.
questions.a: Two numbers add up to 0 only when one is the inverse of the other. The inverses of the faces are 1, -2, 3, -4, 5 and -6, and none of these is on a die. So no pair of faces is a number and its inverse, and the sum can never be 0.
s: States that a sum of 0 needs a number and its inverse
Lists the inverses 1, -2, 3, -4, 5, -6 and notes none is a face
Concludes that the sum 0 is impossible

questions.q:
Assertion (A): In a 3 by 3 border integer square, changing only the number in the centre cell does not change the border sum.
Reason (R): The centre cell is not in the top row, the bottom row, the leftmost column or the rightmost column.
questions.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

questions.q:
Here are six integer cards: (+4), (-11), (+9), (-3), (+15), (-6).
(a) Pick two cards and add them. What is the smallest sum you can get?
(b) Pick two different cards and subtract one from the other. What is the largest value you can get?
(c) Find the sum of all six cards.
(d) Use all six cards, but subtract exactly one card instead of adding it. Which card must be subtracted to make the value exactly 0? Show your check.
questions.a: (a) (-11) + (-6) = -17. (b) (+15) - (-11) = 26. (c) 4 - 11 + 9 - 3 + 15 - 6 = 8. (d) Subtracting a card instead of adding it lowers the total by twice that card, so 8 - 2 x (card) = 0 needs the card +4. Check: (-11) + (+9) + (-3) + (+15) + (-6) - (+4) = 0.
s: (d) Chooses the card +4 with a reason

questions.q: In which year did Brahmagupta give his rules for positive numbers, negative numbers and zero in the Brahma-sphuta-siddhanta?
questions.a: 628 CE

questions.q: In the Chinese work The Nine Chapters on Mathematical Art, how were positive and negative numbers shown?
questions.a: With red and black rods
o: With a special symbol placed after the number
With a minus sign placed before the number

questions.q:
Match each work in Column I with what the chapter says about it in Column II.
Column I: I. The Nine Chapters on Mathematical Art  II. Kautilya's Arthashastra  III. The Bakhshali manuscript  IV. The Brahma-sphuta-siddhanta
Column II: A. Rules for adding and subtracting positive numbers, negative numbers and zero  B. A negative number written with a special symbol after the number  C. Positive and negative numbers shown with red and black rods  D. Credit and debit, and the idea that an account balance could be negative
questions.a: I-C, II-D, III-B, IV-A

questions.q: (a) State Brahmagupta's rule for adding two negative numbers. (b) Use it to find (-13) + (-29).
questions.a: (a) The sum of two negatives is negative: add the numbers without their signs and then place a minus sign. (b) 13 + 29 = 42, so (-13) + (-29) = -42.
s: (a) States the rule: add the numbers without signs and put a minus sign

questions.q: True or false: By Brahmagupta's rules, subtracting a number from zero gives the inverse of that number, so 0 - (-9) = 9. Give the reason or the correct statement.
questions.a: True. Brahmagupta's rule says that subtracting a number from zero gives the number's inverse. The inverse of -9 is 9, so 0 - (-9) = 9.
s: Reason: 0 minus a number gives its inverse, and the inverse of -9 is 9

questions.q:
Use Brahmagupta's rules and name the rule you use each time.
(a) Find (-16) + 9.
(b) Find 9 - 16.
(c) Explain why (a) and (b) give the same answer.
questions.a: (a) Rule for adding a positive and a negative number: 16 - 9 = 7, and the greater number (16) is negative, so the answer is -7. (b) Rule for subtracting a larger positive from a smaller positive: the result is negative, 9 - 16 = -7. (c) Subtracting 16 is the same as adding its inverse -16, so 9 - 16 = 9 + (-16), which is the same sum as (-16) + 9 in the other order.
s: (a) Finds -7 and names the positive-plus-negative rule
(b) Finds -7 and names the larger-from-smaller subtraction rule
(c) Explains that 9 - 16 = 9 + (-16), the same sum as (a)

questions.q:
Assertion (A): By Brahmagupta's rule, 6 + (-15) = +9.
Reason (R): To add a positive number and a negative number, subtract the smaller number (without the sign) from the greater number (without the sign), and place the sign of the greater number.
questions.a: A is false but R is true.
o: A is false but R is true.
Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements.
I. Brahmagupta was the first to describe zero as a number on an equal footing with positive and negative numbers.
II. Negative numbers were accepted by most European mathematicians as soon as they reached Europe in the 13th century.
III. Zero and negative numbers reached the Arab world by the 9th century, before they reached Europe.
Which of the statements are correct?
questions.a: I and III only

questions.q: Kavya says, 'For 4 - (-3), Brahmagupta's rule for subtracting a negative number and the token model give the same answer.' Work out 4 - (-3) both ways and say whether she is right.
questions.a: Brahmagupta's rule: subtracting a negative number is the same as adding the corresponding positive number, so 4 - (-3) = 4 + 3 = 7. Tokens: start with 4 green; there are no red tokens to take away, so put in 3 zero pairs (7 green, 3 red) and take out the 3 red, leaving 7 green, which is +7. Both give 7, so Kavya is right.
s: Uses tokens: puts in 3 zero pairs, removes 3 red, gets +7

questions.q:
Class 6 in Jaipur is making a wall chart called 'Brahmagupta's rules in action'. It must show one CORRECT example for each of three rules: (1) adding a positive and a negative number, (2) subtracting a negative number, and (3) subtracting a number from zero. Students have handed in five cards: P: (-8) + (-5) = -13; Q: 4 + (-10) = +6; R: 7 - (-2) = 9; S: 0 - (-6) = -6; T: (-3) + 11 = 8.
(a) Which of Brahmagupta's rules does card P use, and is it correct?
(b) Check cards Q and T.
(c) Check cards R and S.
(d) Which cards should go on the chart, and for which rule must the class write a new card? Write that card correctly.
questions.a: (a) P adds two negatives (add 8 and 5, put a minus sign): -13 is correct, but this rule is not one of the three on the chart. (b) Q is wrong: 10 - 4 = 6 and the greater number is negative, so 4 + (-10) = -6. T is correct: 11 - 3 = 8, with the sign of 11, so +8. (c) R is correct: 7 - (-2) = 7 + 2 = 9. S is wrong: subtracting a number from zero gives its inverse, so 0 - (-6) = 6. (d) Put T for rule (1) and R for rule (2). No correct card is left for rule (3), so the class writes a new one, for example 0 - (-6) = 6.
s: (a) Names the rule for adding two negatives and says P is correct
(b) Finds Q wrong (answer -6) and T correct
(c) Finds R correct and S wrong (answer 6)
(d) Chooses T and R, and writes a correct new card for rule (3) such as 0 - (-6) = 6
